thread:
karen: Quick heads-up from the onboarding session: several people hit copy/paste issues in the quickstart.
karen: Main two: the README shows a backslash-multiline curl (breaks in PowerShell) and different samples use different env var names (`REDWOOD_KEY`, `REDWOOD_API`, `REDWOOD_API_KEY`).
omar: Oof. Which snippet did they paste?
karen: This one (exact from README):
```
curl \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
karen: Pasting into PowerShell results in `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: -H` or weird parsing. New hires get stuck for 10+ minutes.
paul: Thanks for filing. Two-pronged fix: (A) change README to a single-line, cross-platform curl example and mark multiline as bash-only, (B) pick a canonical env var and update all language snippets.
omar: Which env var should we standardize on? I vote `REDWOOD_API_KEY` for clarity.
paul: Agreed. Also the TypeScript example in docs currently uses a default import that fails for teams with `esModuleInterop: false`. Current README shows `import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference'`.
karen: Right. Several new hires with stricter tsconfig ran into `Cannot find module` or runtime import differences.
paul: Plan: update TS/JS docs to show both forms and a tiny note. Example: `// With esModuleInterop: true` then `import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference'` and `// Without esModuleInterop` then `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'`. Also update sample app to read `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
omar: For curl we should show:
Single-line portable curl:
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
And a PowerShell snippet with Invoke-RestMethod:
```
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY"; "Content-Type" = "application/json" }
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -Method Post -Headers $headers -Body '{"input":"hello"}'
```
karen: Nice. Can we also add a tiny non-network smoke check in docs CI that runs the node example (reads the env var and prints a success line) and a grep lint to assert the README uses `REDWOOD_API_KEY`? That would catch copy/paste rot.
paul: I'll make a docs PR that updates README, normalizes env var across examples, adds the TS import note, and drops `docs/examples/quickstart-smoke.js` that just validates `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` is set and prints "ok".
docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/856 7 files changed  description: quickstart snippet fixes + smoke script + CI lint.
lee: Can we follow up with a sweep for other language samples (python, go, ruby) to ensure they all reference REDWOOD_API_KEY? Small issue to track that would be helpful.
paul: Filing follow-up issue after PR merges. Ill also add a note in the onboarding checklist about the canonical env var and the PowerShell tip.
karen: Thanks everyone. If PR lands ping me and I'll run the onboarding lab again to confirm the flow is smooth. :thumbsup:
